newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HMO stocks hit by fears of premium cuts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HMO stocks hit by fears of premium cuts.

text.p: Shares of U.S. health maintenance organizations tumbled on Monday, spooked by fears that the U.S. government would take steps to slow HMO premium growth rates, analysts said.
The Washington Post reported on Sunday the White House was considering substantial cuts in premiums Medicare paid HMOs, in order to keep federal health insurance programs for the elderly running.
The proposed reductions would, if adopted, cut an estimated $20 billion from HMO premiums over the next five years, the paper said, citing administration sources.
"The White House has been talking about Medicare premium cuts it wants to effectuate," Gary Frazier, an analyst at Bear Stearns, said. "For the first time, we're getting some quantification."

Aetna Inc closed off 2-7/8 at 74-7/8, Oxford Health Plans Inc closed off 2-3/8 at 55-3/8, PacifiCare Health Systems Inc closed off 3-15/16 at 74-5/16 and United Healthcare Corp closed off 1-3/4 at 44-1/4.
PacifiCare had the most exposure to cuts in these premiums, analysts said.
"But these cuts, if they are done, will be over several years," Peter Costa, an analyst at Chicago Corp, said.
Frazier said while cuts of $20 billion over the next five years equated to a 13 percent reduction in HMO premium growth rates, he forecasted a five to six percent growth slowdown.
"But the stocks could still be volatile," he said.
Analysts said part of the proposals called for removing graduate medical education payments and disproportionate share payments from HMO Medicare rates calculations.
